cells.tense: The pattern is already in your hands and you are holding it here with the pen.
cells.act: calibrate what you say to what can be heard
cells.ask: Next time the pattern is in your hands with someone, say the piece they can hear today, and hold the rest until there is room.
cells.core:
You strip a thing down to its pattern, and the pattern turns out to move people — that is the part you are good at. You find what connects underneath the details, you carry it to someone still learning it, and they leave with something they can use. The shape is small enough to hold. You hand over the pattern, not the mess.

What keeps it clean: ask what this person can actually take in today, then say only that piece — not the whole thing, the live edge of it. The rest stays back until there is room. Holding back is not the same as withholding; it is giving the right size. That is what your quiet care does when it is working.
cells.sheetLine: You hand over the pattern in the dose the person can hold.
cells.verb: to carry a pattern until it moves people
cells.place: on the bridge where the pattern is stripped down to itself

cells.tense: The whole pattern is being built out past anyone who could walk it.
cells.act: move the structure one real inch
cells.ask: Pick the one smallest true thing this pattern needs next — one real inch — and do that today, in the world, before you explain anything.
cells.core:
You can see the pattern so clearly that you have started building it out past the people who would live in it. Every meaning goes in before it has been tested, every teaching gets delivered before anyone asked to learn. The reach is real. The stakes have gotten bigger than the room. What was transmission has become force — and the person on the other end is getting the finished building without a say in the plan.

Come back to what can actually be built. Pick one real inch — the smallest true move this pattern needs next — and make that, in the world, before explaining anything. Slow is not failure here. The pattern will go on meaning what it means. You can build it one true piece at a time.
cells.sheetLine: You're finishing the building before anyone asked to live in it.
cells.verb: to carry a pattern until it moves people
cells.place: on the bridge where the pattern is stripped down to itself

cells.tense: You were the one who carried the pattern, and that is over now.
cells.act: cut to the logic and act on it
cells.ask: Take one piece of the pattern you already understand, cut straight to the single step it implies, and do that step once.
cells.core:
The pattern is right there and your hands are not on it. You can still see how a thing connects to the thing beside it, how meaning travels, how people change when they find words for what they feel. That recognition is not gone. What is gone is the walking toward anyone with it. You watch from the edge of the bridge. Meaning happens in a room you are not in.

Start small and clean. Take one piece of the pattern you already understand — not the whole of it — and cut straight to the single next step it implies, then do that step once. Sharp thinking is what charges you; do it moving, not waiting. One piece, one step, and the bridge under you shows itself.
cells.sheetLine: You can still see the pattern, and you've stopped walking it to anyone.
cells.verb: to carry a pattern until it moves people
cells.place: on the bridge where the pattern is stripped down to itself

cells.tense: The pattern is moving under names that are not yours, and yours is absent.
cells.act: say the hard thing gently, once
cells.ask: Say the true thing you see here, the hard part included, once and plainly, as something you see — then let it stand.
cells.core:
Something is moving under people's feet and if someone wrote down who put it there, your name would be missing. The way you take a tangle and find the pattern under it, the way you say the true thing in a shape someone can carry — that is what is holding this together. Told from your side, you were just watching, or just talking. The pattern is yours. The credit is standing somewhere else.

Start by claiming one true sentence. Say what you actually see — the hard part included — as something you see, without softening it into a question, and then let it stand where you put it. What you do with complexity has your handwriting on it. Say so, once.
cells.sheetLine: The pattern under their feet is yours, and nobody has said so.

cells.place: on the bridge where the pattern is stripped down to itself

attempts.check: The record supports that this signature catalyzes meaning through emotional truth in the Abstraction seat; it does not support any claim about how long the person has been withdrawn or what a past connection cost — Too Little must say where they stand, not what happened. The reader could fairly object that 'the pattern moves people' is not something the record proves; the cells should keep the mechanism as what is observable — the person teaching, ritualizing, charging toward what connects — and let them refuse the rest. The asks survive being wrong because each names one small, camera-visible act from the partner's own list, not a state or feeling; the sentence that would serve me more than them is any line implying the person secretly knows what the pattern means — that is not in the record and stays out.
